name: Esogwa Jubilate Aghachiluru
quote: My UBI journey has been nothing short of inspiring.

I still remember almost not applying because I felt I wasn't ready for the challenge. I questioned whether I knew enough to survive the programme. Somehow, I took the leap, submitted my application, and was accepted.

During the orientation, I kept hearing, "This internship will stretch you." Deep down, I laughed and told myself, "You probably won't even make it through the first week." Yet here I am today, preparing to enter Stage 6. Looking back, I can only smile because this programme has shown me that growth begins where comfort ends.

There were moments I wanted to quit, especially during Stage 3. The tasks were demanding, and I genuinely wondered if I belonged. But every time I felt like giving up, I found encouragement from my fellow interns and the incredible UBI community. Their support reminded me why I started and gave me the strength to keep going.

Before joining UBI, I had about six months of cybersecurity learning. In just a few weeks, this internship accelerated my growth in ways I never imagined. I gained practical experience in incident response, threat hunting, log and evidence analysis, vulnerability assessment, security report writing, governance, and mapping adversary techniques to the MITRE ATT&CK Framework. More importantly, I learned how to think like a SOC analyst instead of simply learning cybersecurity concepts.
UBI is more than an internship. It is a place where potential is challenged, resilience is built, and careers begin to take shape.

quote: I want to sincerely thank Quadri Omoloju, Somto Okoma, Benedicta, and the entire programme team. They were responsive, encouraging, and genuinely invested in our success. Yes, we saw a little shege along the way, but looking back, those challenges became part of the learning experience and helped us grow because they already know how things work in real time.
The webinars you put together and the resource persons you bring are top notch. The work materials you offer us is next to none.

Overall, this internship confirmed that cybersecurity is the right career for me. I now have stronger technical skills, greater confidence, and a clearer vision for my future. One of the most unexpected rewards was the relationships I built I learnt not just to add people on my LinkedIn, but forming genuine professional connections with mentors and fellow participants. For that, I am truly grateful. UBI… I am because we are! 👌

name: Mercy David
quote: I joined Ubuntu Bridge Initiative's Cohort 1 wanting to find out if I could actually do the work of a SOC analyst, and not just talk about it.

The Sankofa Digital investigation was where that got tested. I had to triage alerts, correlate logs across a SIEM, and map everything back to MITRE ATT&CK, then write it up as a proper incident report, the kind a stakeholder could actually read and act on.
By Stage 2 I was in web application security, working through SQL injection, XSS, SSRF, JWT issues, XXE, and scoring each finding with CVSS 3.1 in a full pentest report.
Stage 3 pushed even further, building STIX 2.1 IOC bundles and forensic reports straight from evidence , the same standard used in real threat intel work.
What stood out to me is that UBI didn't simplify the work to make beginner-friendly, they gave us the real complexity of the job and trusted us to rise to it.
That is what built my confidence to actually call myself a SOC analyst.
If you are considering applying to UBI, please come prepared and determined as you wont just learn concepts, but you will be able to prove you can do the job.
